goal: Test whether two independent four-observation public-outcome windows can detect a rule reversal before activating a learned model, compared with shorter stale calibration.
known_models: Same separately trained normal collect train/0..79 and reversed route-reversed train/300..379 NumericOutcomeMemory.

calibration.probe_method: existing maximum predictive disagreement between two candidate learned models

selection.each_window: Use unchanged smoothed observed-outcome log likelihood and minimum 4 observations/margin >=2.0
selection.confirmed8: Agreeing windows select common model; disagreeing or uncertain => abstain
selection.early4: Only first four, exactly previous early stop baseline

constraints: Every cohort/seed already inspected, not blind validation
Physics and numeric action features remain engineered; two known rules, no third unknown
Calibration in disposable train worlds, harmful actions must be reported
Model agreement does not prove stationary physics, may miss noisy reversals
Abstention counts task failure, not autonomous solution
No live OS/network actions, source model change, promotion or authenticated user permission
Original protocols and previous benchmark results immutable
